A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and complete appendices. v2's appendix sections are retained as A.2–A.5 in v3, following a new empirical section A.1.

before.justification: v2 reports original spectral simulations and experiments on initialized transformer encoders, including rank-collapse curves and architectural comparisons in Figures 1 and 3–7.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds covariance, spectral, and stable-rank measurements in Appendix A.1, Figures 8–11.

M1.justification: The proposed subtraction of uniform attention, its multilayer application, and the alternative SVD-based removal of multiple outliers are unchanged. New experiments vary inputs and model configurations without modifying the proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 extends the orthonormal synthetic-input setting to deliberately non-isometric, unit-length Gaussian tokens in Figure 10. Both versions already use the paper's abstract text and BERT-family encoders; the coverage extension concerns input conditions rather than new application tasks.

E2.justification: The comparisons involving identity attention, LayerNorm, skip connections, and removal of all outliers are retained in Figures 4–7. TinyBert supports a new diagnostic experiment rather than serving as an additional competitor against the proposed fix.

E3.justification: New protocols include replacing RoBERTa word embeddings with random embeddings, testing row-normalized Gaussian inputs at T/d = 0.1, 0.5, 2, and 10, and varying context length in TinyBert with d = 312. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.1 substantially expands robustness analysis by directly testing dependence on the theorem's orthonormal-input and T/d restrictions. Figures 8–11 add embedding controls, covariance diagnostics, and synthetic and encoder experiments beyond these assumptions, complementing v2's architectural and outlier-removal ablations.

E5.justification: v3 newly specifies five-run averaging for Figure 11's stable-rank results and identifies spectra in Figures 8, 9, and 11 as single realizations with consistency observed across runs. v2 provides no comparable empirical run-count disclosures. No increase in runs for retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: Figures 1–7 retain their results. New Figures 8–11 provide targeted confirmations: spectral gaps persist with non-orthogonal inputs and T/d greater than one, while TinyBert's stable rank approaches one as context length grows. Figure 10 additionally shows altered bulk shapes at larger T/d.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, definitions, theorem statements, proofs, and dynamical-isometry derivations are preserved in the renumbered appendices. New Appendix A.1 experimentally probes assumptions without revising the formal guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: identifying rank collapse in width, explaining its spectral origin and interaction with depth, and proposing removal of the spectral gap. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 newly characterizes the proof as a proof of concept and argues that orthonormal inputs and T/d restrictions are unnecessary for the observed phenomena in practice. This adds an explicit interpretation of applicability beyond the unchanged formal assumptions.

D1.justification: The code footnote changes from a shortened link targeting anonymous code to a named GitHub repository. New captions document input generation, embedding replacement, dimensions, and context lengths. The original implementation section is otherwise retained as A.5.

R1.justification: The references and substantive research positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to prior rank-collapse analyses, centered self-attention, and Differential Transformer.

P1.justification: v3 adds Appendix A.1 and acknowledgements, updates the appendix roadmap, reorders the first two authors, and makes isolated wording edits. Most prose is unchanged. The new appendix contains a reversed context-length heading and an incorrect Figure 10 reference for TinyBert.

P2.justification: The appendix gains substantial new visual evidence: covariance heatmaps paired with spectra in Figures 8–9, a four-panel ratio sweep in Figure 10, and paired spectrum/rank plots in Figure 11. Existing Figures 1–7 remain unchanged. Figure 11's caption incorrectly describes its side-by-side panels as top and bottom.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.1 strengthens practical relevance by directly testing non-orthogonal inputs and T greater than d, extending v2's empirical support without changing its scientific core. Explicit run reporting also helps assess the new evidence. These limited gains outweigh the new section's confusing inequality heading and incorrect figure references.
